newsitem.title: USA: N.C. man found guilty of killing nine women.
newsitem.headline: N.C. man found guilty of killing nine women.

text.p: Confessed serial killer Henry Wallace was convicted Tuesday of murdering nine women, all co-workers at Charlotte-area fast food restaurants, friends of his sister or friends of a former girlfriend.

It took the jury more than 15 hours over four days to reach the unanimous verdict on the nine first-degree murder counts. Wallace, 31, was also convicted of eight counts of first-degree rape, one count of second-degree rape, and 11 other charges of robbery, sexual offence and assault.
Prosecutors have said they will seek the death penalty in the case in a separate proceeding before the same jury of seven women and five men and the same judge.
Wallace sat in Mecklenburg County Superior Court between his public defender and his private attorney with hands clasped and stared quietly at the clerk as she read the verdict.
Victims' family members held hands as the verdict was read. One wept openly, another thumbed through a Bible. Later, they hugged each other and prosecutors Marsha Goodenow and Anne Tompkins.

Wallace was arrested in March 1994 and gave police taped statements detailing how he had murdered 10 women in Charlotte, most through strangulation after raping them in their homes. Tuesday's verdict was for nine of the 10 deaths.
The other, in which the victim was beaten, will be handled in a separate trial.
Dee Sumpter, whose daughter Shawna was left submerged in a tub full of water, said the jury rendered the only proper justice. "I miss my Shawna more today than ever before," she said.
Lawyers on both sides were due to make arguments later Tuesday about when to start the sentencing phase.
